claims.statement: Creation guide covers FPT/GHEC/GHES and supports new or existing repositories; unrelated repository files can be excluded through branch/folder selection or a custom workflow. GHES custom Actions publishing requires site administrator enablement.

Included FPT/GHEC rule requires public repositories for Free user/team accounts. Repository visibility selection is distinct from Pages site visibility; private repository content can still be publicly published.

User/organization site repository name must match lowercased account name followed by .github.io. GHEC managed users can publish only from organization-owned repositories; naming advice alone does not override the separate managed-user project-site restrictions.
New repository instructions select owner, visibility, Add README and Create repository. These UI steps do not authorize creating repositories, accepting costs or publishing content in this estate.

Pages entry file can be index.html, index.md or README.md. With branch/folder publishing it must be at the top level of the selected source folder on the selected branch; main/docs is an example rather than universal configuration.

Actions publishing requires the entry file at the top level of the deployed artifact; the workflow may generate it instead of storing it in the repository. Repository file existence alone cannot verify artifact layout or served entry behavior.

Creation requires configuring the publishing source; the build-pages-with-actions include applies to FPT/GHEC and directs checking actual build/deployment runs. Private/internal Actions usage beyond free minutes can incur charges; source text is not current pricing or cost approval.

The GHEC conditional offers public/private site visibility for project sites from private/internal repositories, with organization GHEC availability prerequisite. UI choice and repository privacy are not independently verified effective reader restrictions.

Visit site is the documented viewing action. Included delay note says up to ten minutes after push and troubleshooting after an hour despite its twenty-minutes filename; neither time statement is a live availability receipt.

Branch publication troubleshooting requires admin with verified-email push and excludes builds from workflow pushes using GITHUB_TOKEN. Generic statements about pushed static files must be qualified by source selection, triggering and successful deployment.

Branch publishing defaults to Jekyll. For another static generator, Actions is recommended; alternatively .nojekyll at publishing-source root disables Jekyll while a separate local build generates files. The marker alone does not perform a build or prove correctness.
Pages serves static output and does not execute server-side PHP, Ruby or Python. Using those languages to generate static files is distinct from server-side runtime support.

Source reports more than 750 MIME types derived from mime-db and disallows per-file/per-repository custom MIME assignments. Upstream mime-db contribution is not immediate installation or proof of current response headers.

Source-folder directory structure maps to served paths, with Markdown conversion example and different cloud versus GHES URL templates. File presence and example URLs do not verify deployed routes, custom-domain behavior or absence of content exposure.

Theme and further-reading links are navigation, not review of linked pages. All claims remain pinned-source reference evidence; no policy adoption, rights clearance, native deployment or exhaustive published-content assurance is certified.
